transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Well, to be completely honest, it’s a bit of a long story, but I suppose the main thing that brings me in today is this... this constant restless feeling I’ve been dealing with. It’s just always there in the background. It feels exactly like I’m wound way too tight, like a toy that's been cranked up too much, and I just can’t fully settle. 

And I mean, I really try to. I work as a wholesale buyer, so my days are usually full of these incredibly long, drawn-out seasonal planning meetings where you just have to sit there and look attentive while someone goes over vendor contracts or supply chain logistics. And I just can't settle into my chair. I'm constantly shifting or feeling this urge to move. 

But it’s not even just at work where it’s a problem, which is why I finally decided to make an appointment. I try to do things on my own time that are supposed to be relaxing, you know? Like, I took up painting recently to try and give myself a creative outlet, and I’ve been going to this yoga class on Thursday evenings because everyone says it's so good for finding your center and unwinding. But even then, when I’m supposed to be calmly sitting there, whether I'm painting a canvas or just doing yoga and trying to breathe, I just have this tight, restless energy. I can't just relax and let go. It’s like my body completely refuses to just sit still and be calm, and it’s just getting so frustrating trying to manage it all the time when I just want to enjoy a quiet moment.
Has this difficulty sitting still and feeling restless been present since you were a child, or did it start more recently in adulthood?

Oh, it’s definitely not a new thing, not at all. I mean, if I really think back on it, it’s been this way for as long as I can remember. Honestly, it goes all the way back to when I was a little girl. I remember—gosh, this must have been second or third grade—my poor mother was always getting these notes sent home from my teachers. And they were always about the exact same things. I was constantly popping out of my seat during lessons. Like, the teacher would be up at the chalkboard explaining fractions or whatever, and I’d just be up, wandering over to the pencil sharpener or looking out the window, just unable to stay glued to that little wooden chair. 

And it wasn't just the standing up, either. I was always talking over my classmates. If someone else was called on, I’d just blurt out whatever was on my mind because I couldn’t wait my turn. I just had this overwhelming urge to get the words out right that second. And if the teacher was asking a question, I’d be shouting out the answer before she even finished her sentence. I just... I couldn't hold it in. It was like my brain was moving a million miles a minute and my mouth and body were just trying to keep up. So, yes, to answer your question, this whole feeling of being restless and just unable to sit still and wait, it’s been a part of my life since I was a kid. It’s just that now, as a 51-year-old woman in a corporate meeting, it looks a little different than a kid jumping up in the middle of spelling practice, you know? But the internal feeling... that’s exactly the same.
Along with that restlessness, do you also struggle with paying close attention to details or staying focused on tasks?

Well, you know, it’s funny you ask that, because for a long time I would have said no, I’m great at my job, I know what I’m doing. But honestly, over the past couple of years... it’s been getting a little embarrassing, to be quite frank. I’ll be looking at these massive vendor spreadsheets—and I mean, they are huge, hundreds of lines of data, pricing tiers, delivery windows, all of that. And I’ll sit there, and I’ll go through it, and I will genuinely think I’ve checked it so carefully. I’ll think, "Okay, this is perfect, ready to go." 

But then, sure enough, our planning coordinator—she’s wonderful, very sharp, bless her heart—she’ll come back to me and point out these little things I just totally glossed over. Like, I’ll have transposed a SKU number, just flipped two digits around without even realizing it. Or I’ll completely miss a freight surcharge buried in the terms, which obviously throws off the entire margin calculation. Or, and this one really gets me, I’ll carry the wrong quantity over into the final purchase order. Like, I meant to order 500 units, but somehow I typed 50, or 5,000, because I just... I don't know, my eyes just sort of slide right past the details. It’s incredibly frustrating because I know the business inside and out, I know how to negotiate, I know what products we need, but when it comes to just sitting there and staring at the tiny numbers and making sure every single detail is exactly right... my brain just kind of skips ahead. I just can't seem to lock in on those little specifics lately without making these silly, careless errors.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits chronic, pervasive symptoms of both inattention (frequent careless errors, difficulty sustaining attention to details in spreadsheets and purchase orders) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (constant inner restlessness, inability to sit still during meetings or relax during leisure activities, childhood history of leaving seat, blurting out answers, and interrupting others). Symptoms have been present continuously since childhood (elementary school, well before age 12) and cause functional impairment across multiple domains (occupational and personal/leisure), meeting criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Combined Presentation (ICD-10-CM F90.2).
